generator.rule: an item is open until a person writes a claim about it
generator.claims_are_never_generated: a claim is what a person asserted. It is read from the register and never written here, because a claim written into a generated document is erased by the next run.
generator.open_is_the_absence_of_a_claim: an item nobody has judged carries no claim block. That is a different fact from one somebody looked at and let go.
generator.addresses: each item addresses its subject with a kind from ci/addresses.py, which is closed. There is no loose-end kind: a loose end is always about something the grammar can name.

reading.as_fresh_as: its stalest input; each source's own time is in generator.sources
do_not: do not write a claim into this file -- it is regenerated, and the register at registers/loose-end-claims.yaml is where a decision survives
do not read an absent kind as zero: a source that could not be read is recorded as unknown in generator.sources
do not treat the total as a backlog to burn down. A declared blind spot is a gap somebody chose and wrote down.

loose_ends.title: adr-lint cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether a record is correct, or whether a restatement and its record agree -- it pairs declarations and compares no text. Three of its four sub-checks cannot fire on any ref CI runs against, which is a known finding and not yet fixed. One commit subject is exempt from the vendor-name rule by full SHA -- 35ebca6a, kept as the worked example the rule is taught from -- and check_attribution.py prints that exemption and its reason on every run.

loose_ends.title: ci-tooling-tests cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether a passing test discriminates. A test that passes against the broken tool is inert, and this corpus has shipped two of those -- only a mutation pass finds them, and no gate runs one. For the walkthrough it also cannot see whether a page is worth reading: doctest asserts that an example's printed output is what the page claims, and asserts nothing about whether the example was the one worth showing.

loose_ends.title: commit-signatures cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether the signer is the person named in the author field, beyond what the key attests. It would establish that an attestation exists, which is currently established for nothing.

loose_ends.title: docs-audit cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether a page is true. It builds the site and reads what the build reads, so it finds a page nobody can reach and not a page that is wrong. `uv run qm prose` reads the openings; a person reads the rest.

loose_ends.title: docs-deploy cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether what it published is correct, or whether anybody reads it. It is a deployment, and it is declared for the same reason the draft build is.

loose_ends.title: docs-draft cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Anything -- it is a build, not a check, and it is listed here because a workflow nobody declared is a workflow nobody can rely on. Declaring it says plainly that it refuses nothing.

loose_ends.title: governance-status cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether the document is current. It checks faithfulness to the refs it names, not age -- a document generated from unfetched refs passed this once, which is why the workflow fetches first.

loose_ends.title: namespace-guard cannot see
loose_ends.detail: A branch cut from the wrong parent whose direction is nonetheless legal. `check_pr_base.py` reports the inheritance; nothing fails on it.

loose_ends.title: one-pr-slot cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether the two pull requests are actually related. It counts slots, not subject matter, and the `--per-base` exemption is a glob somebody passes.

loose_ends.title: private-names cannot see
loose_ends.detail: A repository that becomes private after the fact. By records/DRAFT-going-private-is-an-act-with-obligations.md the party who makes a repository private owns removing its name from this corpus, so nothing here watches for the transition: detecting it would need either an organisation-read credential this repository does not hold, or a committed digest list that would be recoverable, since 24 of 33 names are ordinary words of median length 7. It also cannot see history -- two names are published from 2b50bd6 and no forward fix removes them -- and it does not gate a bare-word match in prose, because several private repositories are named after common words and matching those produced 187 findings with no disclosures.

loose_ends.title: registries cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether any registry is complete. Each of these seven checks the entries that exist against their own rules; none can tell that an exemption, a policy, a ledger entry, a lane, a protocol, a curriculum unit or an address case was never written down, and a registry nobody added to is the state all seven report as clean. Nor can it see an address that is well-formed and wrong: the grammar has no idea whether the branch exists. It also cannot see whether a protocol was ever run -- that is reported by `uv run qm protocols` and deliberately never refused -- or whether a curriculum unit's prose is true of the document it cites. Nor is this gate required to merge: it is a candidate for A-main.json's required list and stays off it until it has reported green on a real pull request.

loose_ends.title: reuse-lint cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether the licence asserted is the licence intended, or whether a dependency's licence is compatible with it.

loose_ends.title: rulesets cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether a rule is the right rule. It compares enforcement levels and rule types, not rule parameters, so a required-status-check list that has been emptied on the host reads as a match. It cannot run in CI at all: reading what is applied needs a host credential, and a check that reads a host reds a pull request for a reason its author cannot fix. It also does not read `rule-suites`, which is the log of what an evaluating rule would have blocked and the thing worth reading before promoting one.

loose_ends.title: secret-scan cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Everything about how it is configured. It is an installed application with no workflow file in this repository and no record describing it, so nothing here states what it scans, who can dismiss a finding, or what happens if it is uninstalled. It appears on pull requests and that is the whole of what this corpus knows about it.

loose_ends.title: symlink-integrity cannot see
loose_ends.detail: A rule missing from one of the two genuinely different AGENTS.md files. They are not symlinked to each other, so this check cannot notice them disagreeing.

loose_ends.title: tag-claims cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether the review or the manual test happened -- it reads an annotation a human wrote. It does not gate tag creation, which needs a host-side tag-protection ruleset, and it runs after the tag exists.

loose_ends.title: tag-determinism cannot see
loose_ends.detail: Whether the suite is deterministic. It refuses a run that announces nondeterminism; one that is nondeterministic and silent about it passes. It also says nothing about coverage: a suite asserting little passes as readily as one asserting much.
